x15598y2.author: Homer
x15598y2.label: Clearing the suitors
x15598y2.translation: Then Ulysses tore off his rags, and sprang on to the broad pavement with his bow and his quiver full of arrows. ... "Dogs, did you think that I should not come back from Troy? You have wasted my substance, have forced my women servants to lie with you, and have wooed my wife while I was still living.
x15598y2.translator: Samuel Butler (1900); Greek: A. T. Murray (1919)
x15598y2.reading: The return runs from book Α to Ν; from Ν to Ω Odysseus must secure Ithaca. The suitors are our habits, passions, inner voices and old worldviews, and "killing" them means bringing light to them and integrating them into the newborn consciousness. For Greeks today, she adds, it means clearing the heritage of those who try to appropriate it.

x1tviklw.author: Homer
x1tviklw.label: Waking in Ithaca without knowing it
x1tviklw.translation: Ulysses woke up once more upon his own soil. He had been so long away that he did not know it again; moreover, Jove's daughter Minerva had made it a foggy day, so that people might not know of his having come, and that she might tell him everything without either his wife or his fellow citizens and friends recognising him until he had taken his revenge upon the wicked suitors. ... As she spoke the goddess dispersed the mist and the land appeared. Then Ulysses rejoiced at finding himself again in his own land, and kissed the bounteous soil;
x1tviklw.translator: Samuel Butler (1900); Greek: A. T. Murray (1919)
x1tviklw.reading: "Odysseus does not return to Ithaca; Odysseus wakes up in Ithaca." He was always there and did not recognise it, which is her image for awakening: as long as you still see "something", you have not yet reached Ithaca.
